props.gloss_en: on the first of Adar they make an announcement about the shekalim
and about the kilayim
the kilayim announcement is understood: it is the time of sowing
but the shekalim announcement -- from where do we derive it?
R' Tavi in R' Yoshiya's name: as the verse says, 'this is the burnt-offering of each month in its month' (Bamidbar 28:14)
the Torah said: renew, and bring an offering from the new terumah
and since in Nisan one must offer from the new terumah, we read early, on the first of Adar, so that the shekalim come to the Temple
(proposed, then set aside) whose view is it? not RSBG's -- for RSBG says two weeks
one asks about the laws of Pesach thirty days before Pesach
RSBG: two weeks
on the fifteenth of [Adar] the tables sit in the provinces, and on the twenty-fifth they sit in the Temple
even if you say [the mishnah is] RSBG's: because of the tables, we read early
it is because of the tables that we read early
Rav: [the portion of Shekalim is] 'Command the children of Israel... My offering, My bread'
Shmuel: [it is] 'When you take the count'
there are three terumot: that of the altar for the altar, that of the sockets for the sockets, and that of Temple upkeep for Temple upkeep
it differs: on [other] new moons six read the day's portion and one reads Rosh Chodesh, whereas now all of them read Rosh Chodesh
it differs: on [other] new moons six read the day's portion and one Rosh Chodesh, whereas now three read the day's portion and four read Rosh Chodesh
[the fifth Shabbat's 'they return to their order'] means the order of the Torah portions
[it] means the order of the haftarot, and [on the special Shabbatot] we do read the day's portion
when Rosh Chodesh Adar falls on Shabbat they read the portion of Shekalim and read the haftara of Yehoyada the priest
if it falls on the portion adjacent to it, whether before it or after it, they read it and repeat it
when Rosh Chodesh Adar falls on Shabbat they read 'When you take the count' and read the haftara of Yehoyada the priest
Rosh Chodesh Adar on Shabbat: they take out three Torah scrolls -- one for the day's portion, one for Rosh Chodesh, one for 'When you take the count'
Rosh Chodesh Tevet on Shabbat: they bring three Torah scrolls -- one for the day's portion, one for Rosh Chodesh, one for Chanukah
it is necessary: had it been said only of this [Tevet], [I would say] in that [Adar] he holds like Rav, that Shekalim is 'My offering, My bread' and two scrolls suffice -- so he teaches us
one was said by inference from the other
R' Yitzchak: three read in Rosh Chodesh and one in Chanukah
Rav Dimi of Haifa: three read in Chanukah and one in Rosh Chodesh
for of the frequent and the infrequent, the frequent comes first
what caused the fourth to come? Rosh Chodesh; therefore the fourth must read in Rosh Chodesh
what was concluded about it?
Rav Yosef: one does not take account of Rosh Chodesh
Rabba: one does not take account of Chanukah
and the halakha: one does not take account of Chanukah, and Rosh Chodesh is primary
R' Yitzchak Nappacha: six read from 'And you shall command' to 'When you take', and one from 'When you take' to 'And you shall make'
rather Abaye: six read from 'And you shall command' to 'And you shall make', and one repeats and reads from 'When you take' to 'And you shall make'
rather what must you say? [the baraita's 'repeat'] means repeating it on [two] Shabbatot; here too, repeating it on Shabbatot
R' Yitzchak Nappacha: six read from 'And you shall make' to 'And he assembled', and one reads from 'When you take' to 'And you shall make'
rather Abaye: six read up to 'And he assembled', and one repeats and reads from 'When you take' to 'And you shall make'
if it falls on 'When you take' itself, they read it and repeat it

answered_by.gloss_en: שני: other new moons six and one; now three in the day's portion and four in Rosh Chodesh (= p_shani_tlata_arbaa)

objections.gloss_en: מיתיבי: ... ומפטירין ביהוידע הכהן; בשלמא למאן דאמר כי תשא -- דדמי ליה, דכתיב כסף נפשות ערכו; אלא למאן דאמר את קרבני לחמי, מי דמי?

answered_by.gloss_en: אין -- לבני מערבא דמסקי לדאורייתא בתלת שנין

objections.gloss_en: אמר אביי: אמרי אוקומי הוא דקא מוקמי התם -- people will say they are merely extending [the day's reading] there
מיתיבי: ... קורין אותה וכופלין אותה; בשלמא לאביי ניחא, אלא לרבי יצחק נפחא קשיא! (30a.4)

answered_by.gloss_en: אמר לך רבי יצחק נפחא: ולאביי מי ניחא? תינח לפניה, לאחריה היכי משכחת לה? אלא מאי אית לך למימר: כופלה בשבתות, הכא נמי כופלה בשבתות (30a.6; = p_kofla_beshabbatot)

objections.gloss_en: מתקיף לה אביי: השתא אמרי למפרע הוא דקרי -- now people will say he is reading backwards
